rules.structure: shallow flats near spawning coves and rocky banks
rules.bait: fresh cut shad, chicken liver, or nightcrawlers
rules.sourceNote: Daily Angler catfish system (spring 55 to 70 feeding window, reservoir flats 3 to 10 ft); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio bait list

rules.structure: humps, channel ledges, and deep brush by day; shallow flats at dusk and night
rules.sourceNote: Daily Angler catfish system (summer 70 to 85, reservoir summer layer 15 to 30 plus ft by day on humps, channel ledges, and deep brush, shallow flats at dusk and night; stink bait best at 75 and up)

rules.structure: feeder creek mouths where the water is flowing in
rules.sourceNote: In-Fisherman, Channel Catfish in Reservoirs (Anderson, 2019), guide Stan Liberty: after several inches of rain the lake rose a couple of feet and his creek mouth spot went from its normal 1 ft depth to 5 ft for a day or two, anchored at the mouth on shad guts; point depth rule added in pack version 3

rules.structure: deep basins, scour holes, and channel bends
rules.sourceNote: Goober Time Guide Service blue catfish seasonal table (under 50, 30 to 60 plus ft, deep basins)

rules.structure: warming mud flats and creek mouths beside channels
rules.sourceNote: Goober Time Guide Service blue catfish seasonal table (50 to 70, 3 to 18 ft, warming flats)

rules.structure: shallow warming bays and travel routes along depth contours
rules.sourceNote: In-Fisherman, Joe Shaw's Secrets to Reservoir Flatheads (mid 50s bite starts, April to May feeding 2 to 10 ft, southern Ohio reservoirs)

rules.structure: dense wood, rock piles, riprap, and undercut banks
rules.sourceNote: In-Fisherman, Joe Shaw reservoir flatheads (prespawn feeding around 70, band set 70 to 72, 10 to 15 ft ravine reservoirs); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (spawn at 70, cavities and large objects)

rules.structure: brush, rocks, and vegetation in upper coves
rules.sourceNote: FishUSA crappie spawning guide (black crappie 60 to 64); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (nests 1 to 5 ft in brush, rocks, vegetation)

rules.structure: brushy cover along creek channel migration routes
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (55 degree step: brushy cover 6 to 12 ft along creek channel migration routes)

rules.structure: isolated wood on channel bends along the creek channel migration route
rules.bait: curly tail grubs or live minnows
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (50 degree step: channel wood 12 to 20 ft on the migration route)

rules.structure: channel ledges, standing timber, and breaklines
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (85 to 90 degree step: suspending 18 to 30 ft over channel ledges and timber); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (summer creek channels and roadbeds)

rules.structure: deep channel bends and drop offs with brush
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (40 to 45 degree steps: channels 18 to 40 ft)

rules.structure: brush, rocks, and vegetation in upper coves
rules.sourceNote: FishUSA crappie spawning guide (crappie spawn 60 to 65, black 60 to 64); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (nests 1 to 5 ft)

rules.structure: brushy cover along creek channel migration routes
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (55 degree step: brushy cover 6 to 12 ft along creek channel migration routes)

rules.structure: isolated wood on channel bends along the creek channel migration route
rules.bait: curly tail grubs or live minnows
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (50 degree step: channel wood 12 to 20 ft on the migration route)

rules.structure: channel ledges, standing timber, and breaklines
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (85 to 90 degree step: suspending 18 to 30 ft over channel ledges and timber); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (summer creek channels and roadbeds)

rules.structure: deep channel bends and drop offs with brush
rules.sourceNote: Don Wirth, Crappie by Degrees guide panel (40 to 45 degree steps: channels 18 to 40 ft)

rules.structure: flats just off the river channel
rules.bait: spider rig with a double minnow rig
rules.sourceNote: CrappieNOW, Deer Season Crappie (Huffman), guide Tim Howell: lakes in drawdown in November, crappie just off the river channel out in the flats in 10 to 15 ft of water on a spider rigged double minnow rig; Realtree fall drawdown pattern corroborating; temperature free level trend rule added in pack version 3

rules.structure: flooded cover at the old shoreline, bushes and timber
rules.bait: jigs fished slowly in the cover, or a slip float and minnow
rules.sourceNote: CrappieNOW, Battling High Water (Huffman): crappie near the old shoreline in 8 ft of water, holding 1 to 3 ft under the surface, on slow jigging and slip float minnows; CrappieNOW (Wong) rise tip corroborating; point depth rule added in pack version 3

rules.structure: rocky areas and inlet channels
rules.bait: bright jigs tipped with minnow or nightcrawler
rules.sourceNote: ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (walleye parent spawn 40 to 50; saugeye is the stocked walleye and sauger cross and stages on the parent timing); AA-Fishing Alum Creek Lake fishing report (staging at mid 40s, rocky areas and inlet channels, 5 to 15 ft)

rules.structure: thermocline humps, depressions, and standing timber
rules.sourceNote: UpIce walleye summer depth chart (most hold 15 to 30 ft; trolling chart rows run 65 to 85); Missouri Department of Conservation reservoir walleye (summer thermocline behavior)

rules.structure: ditches and tapering points leading to spawning flats
rules.sourceNote: Kevin VanDam six season bass table via Fishing.info (pre-spawn 48 to 55, ditches and tapering points); Leesville Lake bass guide (pre-spawn staging on the 8 to 12 ft contour at Leesville Lake)

rules.structure: protected flats with sand or gravel
rules.bait: tube, floating worm, or soft jerkbait
rules.sourceNote: Kevin VanDam six season bass table (spawn 55 to 70, nests near 60); ODNR Pond Management Handbook (spawn starts at 60, nests 1 to 6 ft)

rules.structure: flooded brush and cover at the original bank line
rules.sourceNote: Wired2Fish, The Best Way to Fish Flooded Fisheries for Bass (Browning, Ross Barnett Reservoir): targets the original bank line on a rise, 18 inches to two feet, spinnerbait and shallow crankbait; Bassmaster (Brauer, 3 ft or less on flooded brush) corroborating; temperature free level trend rule added in pack version 3

rules.structure: the last cover still in the water, dock fronts and laydown tips on steep banks
rules.bait: topwaters, square bills, or a flipped jig
rules.sourceNote: Bassmaster, Fishing the winter drawdown, Phase One (water falling): Brian Snowden targets bass in depths of 2 to 5 ft at the last cover still in the water, topwaters, square bills, flipped jig; source says bass without splitting species, filed under Largemouth; temperature free level trend rule added in pack version 3

rules.structure: rock points and the first drop off gravel flats
rules.sourceNote: AA-Fishing Alum Creek Lake fishing report (spring feed in the 50s, 3 to 15 ft); Fishing.info smallmouth table (pre-spawn 50 to 60)

rules.structure: gravel flats beside boulders or logs
rules.bait: tube or Ned rig; live hellgrammites or soft craws
rules.sourceNote: ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (spawn 55 to 65, gravel nests 2 to 20 ft, hellgrammite and soft craw baits)

rules.structure: deep points, humps, and channel rock by day; points and vegetation at night
rules.bait: drop shot or Ned rig by day, jigs at night
rules.sourceNote: Fishing.info smallmouth table (summer over 72, deep points and humps by day, night points 15 to 25 ft)

rules.structure: tributary mouths, tailraces, and riprap
rules.sourceNote: Fly Anglers Online white bass (run best over 55, eggs deposited 5 to 10 ft in tributaries and tailraces); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (open water under 30 ft, spinners and minnows)

rules.structure: gravel flats, sunken islands, and open water schools
rules.sourceNote: Fly Anglers Online white bass (summer schools on gravel flats and sunken islands 10 to 20 ft); Fishing.info white bass activity chart (feeds hardest 65 to 80)

rules.structure: vegetation and submerged wood in shallow bays
rules.sourceNote: onX Fish yellow perch guide (spawn 45 to 52); In-Fisherman perch spawning study (eggs under 10 ft, most often 3 to 6 ft, over vegetation and submerged wood); ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (mid April to early May over vegetation)

rules.structure: colony beds on sand or gravel
rules.bait: red worms or wax worms on a small hook
rules.sourceNote: ODNR Sport Fish of Ohio (peak spawn 65 to 70, nests 1 to 4 ft on sand and gravel in colonies)
